title: Almost perfect, just needs a couple more important feature
body:
I needed a organisational app that worked for both Samsung and iPhone so that my partner and I can share tasks. Apple reminders is actually perfect for us but unfortunately it’s not cross platform.

This app takes most of the boxes, but there’s a couple of easy tweaks that would make it perfect. For example when it shows “my day“ there’s no option to filter the tasks so that it only shows to the designated person. When I’m going through my daily checklist, I don’t need to be shown the reminders that are on my partners daily checklist, it just adds noise. Similarly when we have repeating tasks (for example putting the bins out every week once I have ticked off this weeks, it auto populate the task again ready for next week, but then it looks like I’ve still got lots on my to-do list, I don’t want to be shown the upcoming tasks until they’re within the correct timeframe. Otherwise I feel like I’m running behind… Even if the only remaining tasks are later on in the year! I just want to be able to clear my “daily checklist” without that being dependent on future tasks or other people also clearing their daily checklist

Small things, but incredibly frustrating if you’re somebody who wants to visually clear their checklist

title: Great app, but a few suggestions….
body:
This is by the far the best todo list app, out there, by the way.
Well done, team. 👏🏻

The following relates to the iOS app, but you may find that some of the suggestions, could apply to other formats. 

Improvements:
 
Steps:
 
I would like a few choices here about how to display steps.
Maybe we could choose to see incomplete steps, but I would also like the option to just see all steps, underneath each task.
 
So how about the following step display options:
 
Underneath the appropriate task:
 
next step only
incomplete steps 
all steps
 
These display settings would apply to everytask. You should not be able to set these display options on individual tasks.
That would look messy & inconsistent. 

Maybe there could be a little up & down arrow, to toggle the display of steps under its task.
As far as steps notes go, maybe there could be a little notes icon, that allows you to toggle the notes display.
Then we could see the entire task, step, notes tree, all on one screen. 

It’s kind of bad UI, to have to click through to the step each time, especially when the step is combined with all the step ‘call to actions’.
 
Steps note editor:

I would also like a couple more WYSIWYG options in the steps note editor.
 
Could you add:
 
code block
underline
blockquote
font size 
font colour picker
font family

title: Lacking basic features
body:
The application visually looks great, and the way it syncs with Microsoft products across different operating systems is fantastic, but ultimately the application is flawed as it lacks basic functionality that should have been implemented at release.

Scheduled tasks do NOT appear in "My Day". This is quite a big one and has cost me several times. For some reason, the developers refuse to include scheduled tasks in My Day which means you have to check multiple places to ensure that you have done everything that was due for today rather than seeing everything in a single place. Yes, you can add tasks to your day manually, but this is a time consuming inconvenience that shouldn't be required. 

You also cannot plan tasks for the upcoming day without scheduling, which suffers from the same issue mentioned above. Before I go to bed, I want to jot down the things that I want to achieve the next day, and currently there is no way to make it so that when you wake up, your tasks are waiting for you in My Day. Additionally, to schedule each task for a future date, it's a multi step process, meaning if you create many different entries for a specific day it'll take a long time to do. 

It also lacks a Calendar, which is apparently in the works, but has been suggested by the community for almost 4 years now. How has such an important feature not been implemented yet?

Lastly, the widgets lack dark mode support and look outdated which make them look out of place on your Home Screen. Overall it's okay, but currently I see this introducing more frustration and inconvenience than actually helping you boost your productivity. I do not recommend it in its current state even if it is completely free to use.

title: Reluctant Switch from Wunderlist
body:
Preferred Wunderlist and was reluctant to move. Minor things that make a big difference:

1. Overdue tasks no longer have their date in red. I preferred the sense of urgency this created in Wunderlist and made it clear to me when something was urgent.

2. Reminder is not set automatically to the same date as the due date. This is annoying because it means now I have to manually set the date twice and just slows the process.

3. No week view. Having everything ticked off for my week was one of my biggest satisfactions and now it is gone. Instead now things appear on the ‘planned’ page when really it is far too early to put my mind on them, it is nice to get a break.

4. Formatting issues. Sometimes the to-dos cover the title at the top of the page which is wrong. This will get sorted out soon I know but never had this issue on Wunderlist.

5. Backgrounds are slow to change on the to-do list pages.

Overall I am just very displeased with Microsoft. Wunderlist honestly became something so central to everything I do and now downgrades have been introduced to it. If Microsoft To-Do was really that good then it should have been able to convert Wunderlist users by itself and not forcefully. Really sad to say but really shame on Microsoft for not contributing to an advance in technology and instead really being a detriment to it in my opinion.

title: Simply awful. Find a different ToDo app.
body:
TL;DR: Find a different app to replace Wunderlist, don’t use or even bother downloading this crippled dross. 

Wish I could review with no stars. Unintuitive, difficult, slow as molasses, needs you to create a Microsoft account. (Why? What’s so important for M$ to know when I’m cleaning the oven, sorting out my underwear drawer, or getting cheese on a Tuesday - with my name *and* D.O.B attached to it?? No thanks!) 

The kicker, once you get past the fact that this app is now an exercise in collecting more of your data, is that when you create the M$ account, 19 times out of 20 you can’t login anyway, and are sent ‘round and ‘round the login/auth pages getting nowhere. When you can login you can’t share lists with other people and the sync of existing lists across devices is non-existent, not to mention the app is slower than writing out your to-do list in foot-high letters with chalk on the pavement. 

Wunderlist was great. It did what it advertised, had bags of reliability and functionality for years; I’ve been using it a long time because it was the best out there for years. Along came Microsoft to buy out a good idea and make it their own - and then cripple the app and name they purchased.

I hope the Wunderlist creators are happy with their M$ buyout, and let’s face it, they likely had a pretty penny from M$ to sell and walk away. 

As for M$, I hope you’re pleased to put out this dross, crippled app that does not work. It’s quite an achievement to break a perfectly good and useable app on purpose. 

Wunderlist did *not* need rewriting and turned into an awful piece of broken, data-mining shovelware. 

Mourn Wunderlist and find a different to-do app that isn’t this one. Your heart and mind will be much lighter and free from this frustrating, awful disappointment.

There are no sub tasks (that’s pretty basic for a gtd service); there is no dedicated Mac app; there is a weird ‘your day’ function but it barely works with the rest of the categories you set up; you need to have an Outlook account; you cannot add attachments - and the colours options are both hideous and limited. I can think of no way on which this is better, and several in which it is much, much worse. 

I usually only leave positive reviews, but I’m annoyed about this as it’s so unnecessary - MS could have simply left things as they were rather than spending two years chiselling away at functionality. 

Don’t download this. Or as it’s free download it, laugh at it, then delete it and find something better. It won’t be difficult.

So, after downloading To Do and logging in with my O365 Account. Within seconds, I can see my Tasks. Then I created a Task List and a Task on my Phone and BOOOOM. There it was, right there on the Task Manager on my Laptop with Outlook. 

You can not believe how happy I now am. Total Task Management on the go.
